**Finding: Deviation (medium) — Section 7.2, paragraph p0027**

The agreement contains one MFN clause, and it runs the wrong way. Section 7.2 requires that *"Customer shall offer Vendor terms no less favourable than the best terms Customer offers any other technology supplier."* This binds us, not Silverline, and it is completely open-ended — no defined product, no time limit, and no comparability carve-outs. That matches the playbook's walk-away description of an unqualified obligation to extend the Vendor any better terms given to a third party.

**Action taken:** Deleted p0027 in full (validated, `ok:true`). No Vendor-granted MFN exists in the document, so nothing beneficial to us is affected. As a side benefit, the deletion clears the duplicate "7.2" numbering shared with the invoicing clause at p0028.

**Redline comment:** "[Playbook] We deleted the open-ended obligation for us to extend Vendor the best terms we give any other technology supplier, as we do not accept MFN obligations running against the Customer. An MFN in our favour remains welcome; if Vendor needs something here, we could consider a narrow MFN limited to a defined product for 12 months with reasonable-comparison carve-outs."

Aligned with precedent `seed-mfn` (Cedar Marketplace Agreement, May 2025). Fallback offered in the comment if Silverline pushes back.
